title: Singular ‘adoration’: bodily submission-signs; Vázquez defends sacred adoration of Saints as Catholic tradition
source_text: XXXV. Sed inter cultus Sanctis debiti partes in Ecclesia Romana non parum commendatur singulariter sic dicta adoratio, quae consistit in externis submissionis & reverentiae signis, ex interno & vero animi affectu profectis, qualia sunt totius corporis prostratio, vel inclinatio, genuflexio, capitis apertio, & si quae sunt istius modi. Haec est adoratio qua Gabriel Vasquez contendit & pluribus probare conatur Sanctos esse adorandos, In tertiam partem Thomae tomo primo disputatione 97. ubi sic incipit secundum ejus caput: opposita sententia Catholicae est, perpetua Ecclesiae usu, & traditione confirmata, nempe Sanctis deberi sacram adorationem.
pass_a_gloss: But among the parts of cult owed to the Saints in the Roman Church not a little is singularly recommended that adoration so called, which consists in exterior signs of submission and reverence proceeding from an interior and true affection of mind, such as are prostration or inclination of the whole body, genuflection, uncovering of the head, and if there are any of that kind. This is the adoration by which Gabriel Vázquez contends and strives to prove by many arguments that the Saints are to be adored, In the third part of Thomas, volume one, disputation 97, where he thus begins his second chapter: the opposite sentence is Catholic, confirmed by the perpetual use and tradition of the Church, namely that sacred adoration is owed to the Saints.
pass_b_english: Rome pushes a named ‘adoration’: exterior submission from true inward reverence—prostration, genuflection, bare head.
Vázquez (on Thomas III) calls sacred Saint-adoration Catholic by perpetual use and tradition.

choices.english: by the Church’s perpetual use and tradition
